tasks.short: Notify supervisors or mechanics of equipment malfunctions

steps.what: Notify supervisors or mechanics of observed equipment malfunctions and explain the immediate situation

tasks.design: Retain the operator's direct notification and explanation, with the {OTHER} textile machine controls available to show the observed condition. No structured fault code or automatic diagnosis is required before the operator contacts the responsible person.
tasks.previous_blocker: An abnormal sound, motion or product condition may need immediate explanation rather than a standard fault label.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing machine indications can support the conversation, but the supplied digest does not demonstrate a saving in this notification task.
tasks.still_hard: The operator must describe an uncertain situation and make sure the responsible person understands it.
tasks.human_edge: The operator connects the observed symptom to its physical context and urgency.
tasks.altitude: Notification duties and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify symptoms before investigating a textile machine
reach.learn: Useful symptom descriptions and machine identification

evidence.claim: Retaining direct explanation of an observed malfunction is a model-knowledge boundary; production dashboards do not establish a saving in this conversation.

assumptions: Boundary starts after the operator observes a concern and ends when it is communicated; ongoing observation and mechanical repair are separate tasks.
The operator produces the symptom description and identifies the machine during fully retained s1. No ready structured malfunction flag or fault code is assumed.
If controls provide no useful indication, the operator describes physical observations directly; all explanation and clarification remain counted.
Test native contact or indication functions before considering custom software. OTHER denotes textile machine controls.
No new record requirement, routing system or automation is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local notification routes and urgency procedures
research_questions: Which symptom details help mechanics avoid a second clarification conversation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with zero incremental upkeep. Direct notification and symptom explanation keep their full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record bobbin production without repeated transcription

steps.what: Count or read completed bobbins and capture their type, job and production period
Record production data in the shift record by copying the checked bobbin entry
Reconcile bobbin totals and types, correct discrepancies and accept the production record

tasks.design: Configure one production-entry form in {OPS_SYSTEM} so the operator captures the checked count once and the shift record is populated without a second transcription. The operator retains counting, type identification and reconciliation; {OTHER} textile machine counters provide readings only where available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper job entries and shift spreadsheets required the same count and type to be copied twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Native production forms can reuse a checked entry and maintain a linked shift record.
tasks.still_hard: A machine count may include rejects or resets and may not identify the correct bobbin type or job.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises the physical output and resolves differences between counters and completed work.
tasks.altitude: Repeated transcription may fall; output identification and record responsibility remain with the operator.

reach.task: Reconcile shift output with completed job quantities

evidence.claim: Lectra Valia Furniture provides production and maintenance dashboards and automatic order processing; this shows adjacent production-record capability, not compatibility with a particular winding machine or measured operator savings.
Replacing duplicate bobbin-entry transcription with a configured production form is a model-knowledge design and requires local confirmation of the baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is operator counting, entry and acceptance, not operating the machine or supervisor reporting. The design applies where job-card data are copied into a shift record; an existing single-entry system has no such gain.

In fully retained s1 the operator produces job id, machine id, reporting period, bobbin type, completed quantity, unit and any counter-reset or rejected-output note. Reading, manual counting and field capture remain fully counted; no pre-existing type or discrepancy code is assumed.

s2 reuses the checked entry from s1. A counter is an optional reading source, not a required interface; without one the operator counts and enters manually in s1. Unclear types and quantities are resolved manually before acceptance.
Test native production forms before custom code. OTHER denotes textile machine controls and counters. Existing counter runtime earns no labour saving.
Record mappings and worker-linked access require local review; additional supervisor and operator upkeep is explicitly counted.
unknowns: Existing form and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Can one checked entry replace repeated copying while retaining clear job and bobbin-type identification?

already_counted.description: Count output and capture exact production fields

incremental.description: Maintain form mappings and investigate entry exceptions
Supervisor maintains job and bobbin-type reference data

approvals.approved_version: Exact production record version, job, machine, period, bobbin types and quantities checked in s3; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60; gross 40 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 32. Range covers an existing single-entry process and limited removal of duplicate shift transcription; physical counts and reconciliation remain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Replace depleted packages with full supply packages

steps.what: Replace depleted supply packages with full packages and check correct physical placement

tasks.design: Retain physical supply-package replacement and placement checking with the operator at the {OTHER} textile machine controls. No software change is proposed for lifting, positioning or checking the actual supply.
tasks.previous_blocker: This task requires physical handling and direct confirmation of the correct package and feed.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital records may describe supplies but do not perform the physical replacement in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect placement or supply choice can disrupt operation despite an accurate stock record.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises the physical package and confirms the feed is correctly restored.
tasks.altitude: Physical work and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate correct material availability at the machine

evidence.claim: Retaining physical package replacement is a model-knowledge boundary; production-record software does not establish a saving in this handling task.

assumptions: Boundary is physical replacement and placement checking, not inventory reporting or material transport from a warehouse.
The operator identifies depletion and package suitability by direct observation and job instructions during s1. No structured depleted or correct-package flag is required.
Unclear identity or placement leads to manual checking with the supervisor, retained at full time. Existing safe handling procedures continue.
Test existing machine functions before any separate project. OTHER denotes textile machine controls; no robotic handling is proposed.
No new automation or capture requirement is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which replacement difficulties arise from physical access or package identification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with no added upkeep. Physical supply replacement retains full time; no paperwork baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe textile operations for defects and shortages

steps.what: Observe operations to detect defects, malfunctions and supply shortages through direct inspection

tasks.design: Retain direct observation of machine operation, textile output and supplies, supported by the {OTHER} textile machine controls. Existing indications do not replace checking physical quality, abnormal operation or actual supply condition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Not every relevant defect or shortage is represented by an instrument reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controls can show operating state, but the digest does not establish reliable automated detection for this exact task.
tasks.still_hard: Small visual, tactile or audible changes may be the first sign of a problem.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises a departure from normal operation in its physical context.
tasks.altitude: Observation duties and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Relate visible textile defects to operating conditions
reach.learn: Defect recognition and limits of machine indications

evidence.claim: Retaining direct textile-operation observation is a model-knowledge boundary; production dashboards do not establish complete defect detection or labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and recognition, ending before notification, repair or supply replacement, which are separately counted tasks.
Physical operation and output provide the observations during s1. The operator interprets them directly; no structured defect, malfunction or low-supply flag is presumed.
If indications are absent or ambiguous, manual inspection and enquiries remain fully counted rather than replaced by inferred status.
Test existing indication functions before custom tools. OTHER denotes textile machine controls; no vision or sensing project is introduced.
No new automation or capture obligation is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which relevant defects are visible only in physical output rather than control readings?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with no added upkeep. Physical observation and defect recognition remain fully counted; existing machine indications earn no saving.
